subject: Sev1: Dedicated customer timeouts — suspected TP hang (Acme AI)
thread_body:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rachel Nguyen <rachel.nguyen@acmeai.com>, Sanjay Desai <sanjay@acmeai.com>, NOC <noc@acmeai.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 17, 2025 at 3:12 AM PST
Subject: Sev1: Dedicated customer timeouts — suspected TP hang (Acme AI)

Marissa — looping you in for rollout/comms alignment.

We have a Sev1 in progress for Acme AI (Dedicated, A100 80GB) starting ~02:41am PT. Symptoms:
- Streaming requests timing out; client reports hung streams (no tokens) rather than explicit errors.
- Correlated with TP replicas (TP=4). GPU util flatlines on 1-2 ranks; no NCCL error surfaced to API.
- Draining/replacing the affected replica recovers temporarily; issue recurs under bursty load.

Immediate mitigation we’ve already applied (approved by oncall):
1) Drain any replica with >90s no progress on decode step (manual).
2) Reduce max concurrent requests per replica from 24 → 12 for the Acme Dedicated pool.
3) Temporarily disable CUDA graph capture for TP replicas (feature flag) if we see repeat stalls in next 30 min.

Customer-facing: Rachel/Sanjay are requesting an ETA for a “real fix” and whether there’s any risk of data corruption (we don’t believe so — appears to be deadlock/stall).

Ask:
- Can you help draft a short update we can send this morning re: mitigation + planned runtime rollout?
- What’s the earliest we can credibly message for canary/hotfix (if we decide to cut 1.18.x)?

I’ll keep this thread tight (this is also tracked in SUP-48321).

— Sean
Sean Gallagher
Director, Site Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference


From: Rachel Nguyen <rachel.nguyen@acmeai.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sanjay Desai <sanjay@acmeai.com>, NOC <noc@acmeai.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 17, 2025 at 3:18 AM PST
Subject: Re: Sev1: Dedicated customer timeouts — suspected TP hang (Acme AI)

Sean — thanks for pulling this in quickly.

Two immediate questions from our side:
1) Can you confirm no partial output / corrupted streams? We’re seeing requests that never terminate and have to be killed client-side.
2) Do you have an ETA on a permanent fix? We can live with reduced concurrency for a day but not for weeks.

We can provide logs if you want. Current workload is a mix of 12–18k context + streaming chat responses, bursty at the top of the hour.

Rachel


From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rachel Nguyen <rachel.nguyen@acmeai.com>, Sanjay Desai <sanjay@acmeai.com>, NOC <noc@acmeai.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 17, 2025 at 3:31 AM PST
Subject: Re: Sev1: Dedicated customer timeouts — suspected TP hang (Acme AI)

Sean — I’m on.

Customer-facing guidance (suggested language):
- “We’re seeing a rare stall in multi-GPU tensor-parallel execution under specific mixed prefill/decode load. This is a liveness issue (requests can hang) and not a correctness issue (no evidence of wrong tokens/partial corruption).”
- “We have safe mitigations in place now (drain stalled replicas + lower concurrency).”

ETA framing:
- If this is the known TP hang signature we’ve been working, we can offer:
  (a) a Dedicated-only hotfix build (runtime 1.18.x) within 48–72 hours *if* we can validate on A100 in canary; or
  (b) a slightly longer path to 1.19 canary with the full instrumentation + watchdog changes.

Given Sev1, I’m in favor of (a) + rolling forward to (b) for full prevention.

On your questions:
- No data corruption: agree we should be explicit.
- Rollout: if we cut a Dedicated-only hotfix, we can schedule a canary to Acme’s pool first with rollback gates.

Let me know what you want me to send, vs you. Happy to draft an email update for Acme and have you forward.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Product, Rollouts & Reliability
Redwood Inference


From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rachel Nguyen <rachel.nguyen@acmeai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Sanjay Desai <sanjay@acmeai.com>, NOC <noc@acmeai.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 17, 2025 at 3:46 AM PST
Subject: Re: Sev1: Dedicated customer timeouts — suspected TP hang (Acme AI)

Rachel — confirming what Marissa said:

1) We do not see evidence of corrupted output. The failure mode here is liveness (request hangs / no progress). When it occurs, the safest response is to abort/drain the affected replica so new requests don’t queue behind it.

2) We’ve applied mitigations now:
- lowering concurrency on the affected pool
- proactively draining replicas that show no decode progress

These should stabilize the service while we roll out a code-level fix.

Next steps / ETA:
- We’re validating whether this matches a known TP stall signature. If so, we can deliver a Dedicated-only hotfix build for canary within ~2–3 days, followed by broader rollout.
- I’ll send another update after we have a confirmed path (by 10am PT at the latest).

If you can share: timestamps for two example request IDs that hung + whether the client disconnected (timeout) vs manually cancelled, that would help us narrow it.

— Sean


From: Sanjay Desai <sanjay@acmeai.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rachel Nguyen <rachel.nguyen@acmeai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, NOC <noc@acmeai.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 17, 2025 at 4:02 AM PST
Subject: Re: Sev1: Dedicated customer timeouts — suspected TP hang (Acme AI)

Thanks Sean.

Two examples (PST):
- 03:21:07 request_id=acme-7f2c… client timeout at 60s (disconnect)
- 03:34:51 request_id=acme-91aa… manual cancel at ~75s after no tokens

We can temporarily reduce concurrency further if needed but it impacts our SLA. Please keep us posted on the hotfix path.

Sanjay


From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rachel Nguyen <rachel.nguyen@acmeai.com>, Sanjay Desai <sanjay@acmeai.com>, NOC <noc@acmeai.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 17, 2025 at 9:14 AM PST
Subject: Re: Sev1: Dedicated customer timeouts — suspected TP hang (Acme AI)

Update from overnight triage:
- Mitigations are working: no new customer pages since we dropped concurrency; we still saw 2 replicas enter the “no progress” state and drained them.
- Pattern aligns with TP decode stall on client disconnect/cancel path (hangs after a streaming cancellation). Matches what we’ve suspected in the TP stability initiative.

Proposed plan to message:
1) Today: keep concurrency cap + proactive drain in place. Optionally enable extra NCCL/debug logging for a short window if we can do it safely (INT-2219).
2) 48–72h: Dedicated-only hotfix canary to Acme with cancellation-path fix + improved error surfacing (so hangs become explicit abort/retry).
3) 1–2w: roll forward to the 1.19 stability bundle (watchdog + scheduler/comms hardening) after canary gates.

Marissa — can you help wordsmith the 48–72h hotfix canary commitment without overpromising? I want to be specific but safe.

Rachel/Sanjay — we’ll send a formal customer update shortly with this plan.

— Sean


From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rachel Nguyen <rachel.nguyen@acmeai.com>, Sanjay Desai <sanjay@acmeai.com>, NOC <noc@acmeai.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 17, 2025 at 9:37 AM PST
Subject: Re: Sev1: Dedicated customer timeouts — suspected TP hang (Acme AI)

Agree with the plan.

Suggested wording for customer email (re: 48–72h):

“Based on initial triage, we believe we’ve identified the stall trigger and have a targeted fix in validation now. Assuming canary validation on equivalent A100 hardware passes and we see no regressions, we expect to begin a Dedicated canary rollout to your environment within the next 2–3 business days. We’ll keep mitigations in place until the canary demonstrates stability, and we have clear rollback criteria.”

We should also add:
- What ‘mitigations’ are (concurrency cap + draining stalled replicas) and that they’re reversible.
- A commitment to a daily status update until canary is complete.

If you want, I can draft a separate “what to expect during canary” paragraph (potential brief replica restarts, no data access changes, etc.).

— Marissa


From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rachel Nguyen <rachel.nguyen@acmeai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Sanjay Desai <sanjay@acmeai.com>, NOC <noc@acmeai.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 17, 2025 at 5:46 PM PST
Subject: Re: Sev1: Dedicated customer timeouts — suspected TP hang (Acme AI)

Rachel/Sanjay — end-of-day update.

Status:
- Service is stable under the current mitigations (reduced concurrency + proactively draining any replica that shows “no progress” in TP decode).
- We believe the trigger is related to a streaming cancellation/disconnect path that can leave a multi-GPU collective waiting. This matches the hang signature we’ve been tracking internally.

Fix + rollout plan:
- Targeted fix is being validated now. If validation passes on A100 canary, we expect to begin a Dedicated canary rollout to your environment within the next 2–3 business days. We will keep mitigations in place until canary results are clean, with explicit rollback criteria.
- Longer-term, we’re rolling forward additional stability work (watchdog + scheduler/collective hardening) as part of our next runtime release.

What we need from you (optional, but helpful):
- If you can share 2–3 more timestamps/request_ids where the client disconnected, that will help us verify we’re hitting the same path in testing.

We’ll send another update tomorrow by noon PT (or sooner if we hit the canary gate earlier).

— Sean
Sean Gallagher
Director, Site Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference
